scope: P15 HTTP/security/PostgreSQL, real isolated Mailpit SMTP, actual Stripe SDK/signature with a loopback provider transport; no external provider credentials or commercial transaction.

history.cause: A local mixed String/UUID Map.of fixture inferred an intersection value type rather than the required Map<String,Object>. Its declaration was made explicit.

observations: Schema12 passed. HTTP11 had one assertion failure and one error.
The method fixture supplied ETag prefix method instead of the established personal-method prefix, causing REVISION_CONFLICT before the ledger assertions.

The short EUR window expected zero but included 2500 from another EUR payment. Relative timestamp ordering was not retained or diagnosed. The endpoint inclusivity test now isolates the sole USD payment, preserving from-inclusive and to-exclusive assertions.

Manual full-period EUR3500/refund400/net3100 and USD3000 values, CSV filters/hash, permissions, draft publication, SMTP recovery and idempotent replay had already passed before those fixture corrections.

history.observation: The pre-existing exhausted-transport test expected DEAD after Thread.sleep(1150) followed by a one-shot drain, but observed RETRY. Detailed persisted attempts/deadline were not retained after cleanup. The new future-predecessor regression passed.

preExecutionCorrections: The order reconciliation receipt now targets kind ORDER/orderId and preserves the actual job state.
Incident idempotency lookup occurs before the filtered incident projection, permitting the same action receipt after its source reaches SENT. Both are asserted through HTTP in the successful run.
boundaries: Only names, timings and result metadata were extracted from JUnit; system properties/stdout/payloads are excluded.
Provider HTTP is an explicit local transport double. PostgreSQL, the pinned SDK/signature, business services, transactions and SMTP/Mailpit are real.
This file does not claim browser, external Stripe, production, deployment or GitHub CI validation.
The first two failures remain documented; neither is reclassified as a successful execution.

firstGlobal.diagnosis: The claim changes only updated_at among the finite/date-order fields of this CHECK. Persisted created_at and expires_at were already valid. The new updated_at was therefore below created_at. The physical clock cause was not diagnosed; the isolated database had been cleaned.

outboxCorrection.behavior: Persisted updated_at never falls below created_at or previous updated_at. SENT/purged_at/updated_at share one clamped SQL timestamp. Lease, retry schedule and expiry deadlines are unchanged. No DDL or historical row rewrite.
outboxCorrection.regression: A valid explicitly inserted future predecessor uses real AES-GCM ciphertext and actual SMTP failure, authorized requeue and Mailpit acceptance; checks immutable creation, bounded timestamps, two attempts and one notification/mail.
outboxCorrection.fixedSleepObservation: The first corrected 33-test run observed RETRY after an old fixed1150ms sleep plus one-shot drain. No detailed persisted attempt/deadline survived cleanup; no physical timing cause is claimed.
outboxCorrection.testWait: The corrected old recovery and exhaustion tests poll the real worker for at most8seconds, preserving backoff/DEAD/two-attempt/permission assertions. Permanent delay still fails with status, attempts, nextAttempt, database time and due metadata only.

subsequentTargetChecks.observation: The deterministic future role-revocation fixture passed. A different existing refund contradiction case encountered stripe_event_inbox_check1 in RefundWorker.failed. Its date-order invariant requires updated_at>=created_at; the initial caught RuntimeException details were not retained. No physical clock cause is claimed.

Future signed envelope claim/apply/processed and SDK retrieval failure paths passed. The independent foreign purchase ended with covers=false despite operation PREPARED, reserved100 and revoked0 assertions passing. The isolated database was cleaned before diagnosis; no cause or fixture JVM issue is claimed.

subsequentTargetChecks.exitCodeObservation: Original execution session was unavailable after context recovery; BUILD SUCCESS and JUnit one-test/zero-failure results were observed concordantly.
subsequentTargetChecks.observation: The foreign-purchase refusal did not reproduce in the single case; no lazy metadata was collected.

The original independent foreign purchase assertion passed without collecting lazy diagnostics. Another expected retained A access returned false at the first covers call in partialConfirmationAndDuplicateSignedRefundEventsApplyOnlyTheSelectedOriginOnce. That assertion had no diagnostic yet; the isolated database was cleaned. Cause unknown; no policy/clock/financial assertion changed and no package or global run followed.

All seven expected retained-access assertions use one real covers call each. Safe PostgreSQL predicates are collected only after a false result; this run produced none. Both earlier refusals remain unexplained, not corrected by a policy or fixture date change.

inboxClockCorrection.behavior: Metadata updated_at is bounded by immutable created_at and its prior value. Terminal processed_at/updated_at share one PostgreSQL instant. Lease, retry deadlines, states, constraints and V014/V015 migrations are unchanged.
inboxClockCorrection.regression: An existing refund case verifies actual signed future-persisted envelopes through claim/apply/PROCESSED and real SDK GET-failure/RETRY, preserving financial assertions and duplicate-event idempotence.

Expected retained A access returned covers=false after partial refund of B. That assertion lacked the newly added lazy diagnostic at this run; database cleaned before diagnosis.

unresolvedAccessFollowUp.guard: No retries of covers, authorization/financial relaxation, grant antedating or asserted clock/JVM cause. Keep the issue for P17/P19 before delivery.
